messages:
maria_g: quick heads-up: bringing up opal-mini-multilang-v2 quantized to int6 (per-channel). Baseline recall@5 for en/fr/ja looked ok on long queries but short queries (<=5 tokens) recall@5 dropped ~5-7% in fr/ja. Anyone seen this before?
sam_k: oh interesting. numbers?
maria_g: run: ./eval.sh --model opal-mini-multilang-v2 --quant int6 --dataset multilingual-shortquery-holdout --metrics recall@1,5,10
output:
EN: R@5 float=0.82 -> int6=0.81
FR: R@5 float=0.78 -> int6=0.71
JA: R@5 float=0.75 -> int6=0.68
(-> baseline float32)
jordan_r: that's pretty big in FR/JA. do we apply per-channel scales? int6 supports per-channel, right?
kevin_t: yes per-channel enabled. are you using the same normalization/pooling? short queries more sensitive to L2-norm shifts.
maria_g: same preprocess pipeline. ran with and without L2 rescale, no change. embedding norms shifted: mean_norm float=1.02 vs int6=0.86 (for ja/fr short queries).
ciara_eval: eval-bot triggered run for sample inspection -> posted example mismatches
eval-bot: sample mismatches for FR:
Query: "Comment ça marche ?"
Top-5 float: [docA, docB, docC, docD, docE]
Top-5 int6:  [docX, docB, docY, docZ, docE]
cosine(float_top1, int6_top1) = 0.88
cosine_normed(float->int6) = 0.76
sam_k: hmm norm change explains cosine drop. Can we try epsilon recalibration or per-batch norm correction? maybe quantization scale underestimates for short token length embeddings.
jordan_r: try running with prefix cache disabled? not related but worth excluding runtime stuff.
maria_g: I'll run these in staging. plan:
1) rerun quant with per-layer override scales
2) add post-quant L2 rescaling to match float mean norm
3) run recall sweeps by language and qlen
kevin_t: also do centering (subtract mean) check; for multilingual short queries mean shift can hurt.
maria_g: starting run 4212345700 (pings)
cmd:
```
python eval_embeddings.py --model opal-mini-multilang-v2 --quant int6 \\
  --post_rescale mean_norm --rescale_target 1.02 \\
  --dataset multilingual-shortquery-holdout --langs fr,ja,en
```
eval-bot: run 4212345700 complete: FR R@5 restored to 0.76 (still -2% vs float), JA 0.73, EN 0.82
notes: rescale helped but didn't fully close gap.
ciara_eval: :thumbsup: good start. Can we add a small finetune (adapter) on short queries? even 10k examples might fix.
sam_k: ops: what about using quant4 or int4 maybe distort more; int6 seems ok but tuning needed.
maria_g: agree. filing follow-up: create short-query-adapter experiment and try per-lang rescale constants. I'll open a ticket. cc @kevin_t @jordan_r
kevin_t: SG. Also flagging to ENG-Serving: ensure runtime doesn't apply unintended FP32->FP16 conversion before quantized path. saw that once.
jordan_r: thanks. If anyone else wants to poke at the eval set, it's here: s3://redwood-evals/multilingual/shortquery-holdout/
maria_g: thanks all. leaving notes in ticket and summary in repo README. will report back with adapter numbers.
